title: TICTeC presents: Digital Democracy Edinburgh
content:
Here’s something to look forward to in 2027! Put the date in your diary now, and get set to join us in one of the UK’s most beautiful cities, for two days of exploring how digital tools can help make democratic systems more effective, inclusive and participatory.

Bringing together international approaches as well as local innovation from Scotland and across the UK, the conference will showcase and connect some of the most exciting thinking and practice in digital democracy.

We’ll share details of registration, and an open call for proposals, in the next few weeks, with opportunities for researchers, practitioners and others working across these areas to contribute to the programme.

But for now, put 11-12 March 2027 in your calendar, and sign up for updates to hear when further details are announced.

title: They work for you (and we do too)
content:
Dear friend,

Here’s what we’ve been doing recently to make that happen. 

Our alerts service will send you an email whenever your chosen keyword or phrase is mentioned in Parliament; or you can follow any MP or other representative to receive an email when they speak or vote.

So far in 2026, we’ve sent 2.2 million email alerts and our users have created almost 2,000 new keyword alerts through our new and improved alerts management system.

This service helps people understand what their representatives (across all of the UK’s Parliaments) are saying and doing, and also provides an essential service in providing free parliamentary monitoring to civic groups and organisations who can now have as much access to this intel as those with big pockets.

This doesn’t happen by itself: every day our team pulls together the transcripts from the UK's Parliaments, fixing formatting issues and broken files to get these loaded into the site and our alerts.

If you don’t have alerts set up, what are you waiting for? You can do it now at TheyWorkForYou.com.

title: Access To Information in practice
content:
Dear friend,

Join us for one or more of our three webinars this autumn, where you’ll hear practical experiences of delivering, defending and building Access to Information.

Across these sessions, we’ll hear how regulators in the UK and Chile can help people exercise their rights; how civil society in Germany and Mexico is responding to threats and changes to FOI; and what we can learn from building ATI infrastructure in Peru and across Europe.

The series is designed as a space for practical learning and exchange between anyone with an interest in the right to information. It all kicks off on 28 September, International Right to Know Day!

Find out more and book here.

Aiden Clarkson from the UK’s ICO and Christian Anker from Chile’s Council of Transparency discuss what good regulatory support looks like in practice. Find out more and book here.

Veza Clute-Simon and Martin Szyszlican will share what has been happening in their respective countries — and how civil society has responded.

title: Watching 'Buried' with Michael Sheen?
content:
Dear friend,

Have you watched the BBC two-parter Buried, in which actor Michael Sheen follows the evidence around several toxic waste dumps across Wales and England? 

We were very interested to learn that much of the research that informed the programme was obtained via our Freedom of Information site, WhatDoTheyKnow, by a tireless campaigner for the truth — vicar Paul Cawthorne.

We spoke to Paul to learn more about the part FOI has played in bringing this terrible scandal to public attention. Read our conversation here.

This isn’t the first time our sites have played a part in a TV campaign. In October 2023, we spoke to WhatDoTheyKnow user Eleanor Shaikh, who’d uncovered crucial evidence about the Post Office scandal.

In January ’24, the extent of the issue hit the public consciousness via TV series Mr Bates vs the Post Office. You can hear Eleanor explain how she used FOI in this ten minute podcast.

And all the way back in 2011, we built the app for George Martin’s empty homes campaign, the Great British Property Scandal.

That programme is now off air, but you can read more about how we adapted our FixMyStreet codebase so people could report empty buildings in their area.

title: Feeling these heatwaves?
content:
Dear friend ,

It’s been relentless this summer, hasn’t it? These endless heatwaves are a real wake-up call for our councils, showing very clearly that they need to be putting adaptations in place to make our infrastructure more resilient against extreme weather, wildfires and drought.

But don’t sweat. Here’s Isaac from our partners Climate Emergency UK explaining what you can do if you’re feeling powerless in the face of all this heat.

The key is adaptation — the ways in which councils adapt our habitats for resilience, for example by planting more trees, reusing water or making our homes more able to withstand extremes of temperature.

There are useful graphics that explain more on the Council Climate Action Scorecards site. And once you've got that info, take a look to see how your own council is doing, on the main Scorecards section.

While this sun is beating down, it's a great time to go and chat with your councillors about your council's record on adaptation and resilience: why not download these graphics as a conversation-opener?

title: Now WriteToThem is even more helpful
content:
Dear friend ,

We've recently made changes to WriteToThem, our "contact a politician" website, making it easier to do two things:

First, because it can be confusing to figure out which politician to write to, we’ve added new bits of advice that you'll encounter as you use the site, making it easier to get your message to the right person.

And secondly, recognising that WriteToThem has always been an invaluable resource for organisations and charities, we’ve upgraded the options for those using the site to rally support around a campaign (with our usual safeguards around doing so responsibly).

Hop on over to this blog post for all the details.

The improvements described above benefit all WriteToThem users across the UK, but we’ve also been doing work specifically around democratic engagement in Wales.

In a webinar last week, we looked at recent changes to the Senedd, inviting Jess Blair from ERS Cymru to talk through how things look post-election, how the power balance has shifted and how that affects those living in Wales.

After Jess had spoken, mySociety’s Alex explained the changes we’ve made to WriteToThem especially for those with devolved parliaments.

title: AI, government, FOI... and sewage discharges
content:
Dear friend,

Our governments are adopting AI at speed, and we think it should be easier to answer the basic questions: what systems are public bodies using? How are those systems affecting people? Where does accountability lie, when decisions are made in a black box?

We’re embarking on a vital new project, focusing on scrutiny of governments' use of AI. And to kick it off, we brought together experts for an informed discussion about what’s needed. You can read a summary here.

The Information Commissioner’s Office has issued new advice, reflecting the increasing use of AI by those submitting Freedom of Information requests. 

AI brings a new and unique set of challenges to public authorities, many of whom are reporting exceptionally high levels of correspondence. If you'd like to find out how to navigate FOI in this new era of AI, you can read all about it here.

Public opinion does make a difference: it was an increased number of complaints from the public that caused the ICO to take action on sewage data recently, reminding water companies of their obligation to disclose information on discharges: read more here.

title: 39 million moments of civic action 🌟
content:
Dear friend,

As you follow the work we do here at mySociety, we hope you’ll be pleased to see that, in 2026:

  • we empowered millions of people to transform communities
  • we equipped thousands of activists to make real change
  • we helped ensure authorities operate with accountability

    • ... and that’s not all.

  • enabled 82,204 people to engage with political issues
  • released 154,496 previously hidden government documents
  • equipped 3,000+ organisations across the globe
  • facilitated 577,258 neighbourhood issues to be reported and fixed
  • empowered the public to follow the money behind politics
  • resourced 76% of UK councils to tackle the climate emergency
  • prototyped the UK’s first Violence Against Women Data Hub
  • supported 80,015 people to contact their representatives. 43% were writing to a politician for the first time — and 10,800 messages were from people living in the most deprived areas of the UK

    • And overall, there have been 39 million sessions across our websites — 39 million moments of civic action.

title: We have a brand new Prime Minister
content:
Dear friend ,

With all the fuss about Andy Burnham becoming Prime Minister, it may be easy to forget that he’s been in Parliament before — as an MP.

That means that he already had a page on TheyWorkForYou, our website that makes Parliament easier to follow. And, as Burnham originally entered the House in 2001 and didn’t step down until 2017, there’s a lot to explore.

That includes his voting record during that time*.

You can also search Andy Burnham’s speeches, or browse the interests he declared. Of course, all these pages will quickly fill up with new content now that Burnham is Prime Minister.

There’s an easy way to keep up to date with everything that Burnham does in Parliament: click the ‘get email updates’ button at the top of his TheyWorkForYou page, and we’ll send an email when he speaks or votes. This is a free service.

Perhaps you’d like to hear only when he mentions football, railways, wildlife…or anything else you have an interest in. The possibilities are genuinely endless — you can subscribe to as many keywords or phrases as you like.

Here’s how:

  • Go to theyworkforyou.com/alert and click the green button marked ‘create new keyword alert’.
